<b>Die Zahlen:</b> <b>MAE</b> mittlerer: The numbers: MAE mean error in knots · Bias too much or too little forecast, on average · Direction share of hours with at most 45° deviation (only where ≥ 8 kn was measured) · F1 wind how well “over 12 kn in daylight” was hit, 1.0 would be perfect.
<b>Lücken:</b> wie nah die Messung an „j: Gaps: how close the measurement gets to “now” depends on the service. DWD has quality-checked hours up to the day before yesterday and the current day from ten-minute values — yesterday is missing until the next daily file arrives; KNMI goes up to the day before yesterday, Rijkswaterstaat, GeoSphere and DMI up to the current hour, Météo-France up to early this morning. Each spot shows which hours have a measurement; without a measurement, the curve stays empty.
<b>Modelle im Vergleich:</b> jedes Wette: Model comparison: each weather model on its own against the same measurement — the global ones (ICON, ECMWF, the AI model ECMWF-AIFS, GFS, Météo-France, UKMO) and up to three regional models that cover the spot; raw, without wind factor and thermal, while the “Wingfoilscout rating” includes both. Every check goes into the memory (modellguete.json); the ranking across all checks so far is at the bottom. Best model so far: the best one at this spot according to the memory (with at least 24 hours in common), otherwise the best across all spots. The chart fits three lines at once.
<b>Unbrauchbar</b> und <b>fragwürdig</b>: Unusable and questionable come from the shoreline geometry: there, the measured water area doesn’t match the coordinate. Unconfirmed means that the coordinate comes from an imported list and nobody has ever looked at it — for the Takeout list up to about a kilometre off; these are sorted by distance, nearest first.
<b>Was als Wind der Session gilt:</b> di: What counts as the session’s wind: the measurement if the station is at most {km} km away, otherwise the Wingfoilscout forecast; which one was used is shown with each supporting session. A station measures over land at a height of ten metres, on the coast usually less than out on the water. If the measurement is still missing (with DWD, yesterday only arrives with the next daily file), “Compare again” fetches it later.
<b>Was verglichen wird:</b> zu jeder Ses: What is compared: for each session, Wingfoilscout fetches what it would have said for exactly those hours (with regional model, wind factor and thermal — the same calculation as in the Review), what the individual models said and, if there is a weather station within 30 km, what was measured.
<b>Welche Station:</b> „Station bis … km: Which station: “Station up to … km” sets how far from the spot it may be. The nearest one that has almost all hours up to now (90 %) is taken; if none has that many, the nearest one with almost as many as the best. If a closer one was passed over, it is shown alongside. The farther away, the less it says about the spot.
<b>Welche Vorhersage:</b> die aufgehoben: Which forecast: the archived one with the shortest lead time — “today for today”, not the one from three days earlier; for the current day, this morning’s.
<b>Windfaktor:</b> jede Session grenzt i: Wind factor: every session narrows it down — “just right” means the raw model wind of the same hours times the factor was within the range of the wing you rode, underpowered means below it, overpowered above it. The suggestion is the closest factor that fits all of the spot’s sessions (the smallest change that explains them), rounded to 0.05, between {von} and {bis}. Hours with an assumed thermal don’t count for this.
<b>Windfenster:</b> untermotorisiert bei: Wind range: underpowered at a wind that the quiver already lists as suitable for this wing raises the lower limit; overpowered within the range lowers the upper limit; “just right” outside it widens the range.
<b>Wo es liegt:</b> <code>tagebuch.json<: Where it’s stored: tagebuch.json in the Wingfoilscout folder — only on this computer, not on GitHub.
<b>Woher die Messung:</b> DWD (Deutschla: Where the measurement comes from: DWD (Germany), KNMI and Rijkswaterstaat (Netherlands — Rijkswaterstaat measures on the water), GeoSphere (Austria), DMI (Denmark), Météo-France (France); the search crosses borders, so a Belgian spot gets the nearest Dutch station. On top of that, Windguru stations if they are in the configuration with their API password (stationen: windguru: in config.yaml, example in config.example.yaml). A station measures over land at a height of ten metres, while the spot is over water; on the coast it usually measures less than further out.

Wie gut eine Stunde mindestens sein muss: How good an hour needs to be, at minimum, to count as a session. The rating combines wind speed, direction relative to the shore, gustiness and temperature into a number between 0 and 1. 0.55 also lets mediocre hours through, 0.8 shows only the epic days.
Wie gut lagen die Wettermodelle an den b: How well did the weather models do at the best destinations of the last search? For the last few days up to the current hour, Wingfoilscout fetches the measured winds of the nearest weather station and the forecasts as they were at the time. The chart shows the measurement and the range of all models; individual models, the best one so far and the Wingfoilscout rating can be switched on below it.
How much short, steep waves bother you. Wingfoilscout estimates them from the wind’s fetch over the water: lots of open water in front of the spot means lots of chop. 0 = don’t care, 1 = you want flat water.
Wind, Böen, Temperatur, Regen, CAPE und: Wind, gusts, temperature, rain, CAPE and weather code from Open-Meteo (free, non-commercial plan).
Windlage und Wellenhöhe stammen, wo eine: Where a fetch rose exists, wind angle and wave height come from the OpenStreetMap shoreline geometry: fetch over water in 36 directions, giving offshore / side-shore / onshore and the wave height via the fetch-limited SPM relation.

Zusätzlich Regionalmodelle mit 1 bis 2,5: Additionally, regional models with a 1 to 2.5 km grid instead of the 7 to 25 km of the global ones. They resolve valley winds and sea breezes that vanish in the coarse grid — Ora, Maestral, thermals on the Alpine lakes. In return they only reach two to three days ahead; after that, the global ones apply again.
